note: Curated from the Btown Brief newsletter vault (editions Sep 25 - Oct 30, 2026, after a longer-than-usual gap between refreshes). TALKING-POINTS.md is the style doctrine; refreshes land as PRs and points age out via 'added'.

points.text: Some sheep escaped from the Episcopal Diocese down the street and wandered the grounds of the new Burlington High School until diocese staff rounded them up and walked them home. Which animal would you least want to be the one chasing down?

VTrans listed the 1928 Burlington-Winooski bridge, 359 feet long and too big to move in one piece, on Vermont's Craigslist free stuff page, since federal rules require historic bridges go up for free before they're torn down. What would you actually do with a free 359-foot bridge?

Burlington's Robin's Nest Children's Center turned 40 this year, and the community raised $40,000 for it, money going toward educator training, playground upgrades and new flooring. What's the one piece of playground equipment you'd want that money to go toward?

Desmond Tse of Edmonton wore the same pair of Darn Tough socks for 101 days straight without washing them, breaking the old record of 55, and the Waterbury company threw him a ceremony for it. What's the longest you've gone rewearing one piece of gear before admitting it needed a wash?

Scientists at the Vermont Center for Ecostudies are gluing tiny solar-powered trackers onto monarch butterflies, named things like Ann, Scott and Pam, and learning some Vermont monarchs winter in Florida and the Caribbean instead of Mexico. Which butterfly name would you want tracking its way south this year?

Winooski just finished rebuilding nearly 4,000 feet of Main Street after a two-year, $28.3 million project, with new bike lanes, wider sidewalks, 200-plus trees and the utility lines finally moved underground. What's the first thing you noticed walking or driving through?

The Vermont Historical Society has taken in Big Heavy World's entire local music archive, decades of recordings and posters, plus the actual ladle from Nectar's and the door from 242 Main. What object from a gone Burlington venue would you want saved behind glass?

When the Greater Burlington YMCA's lockdown switch accidentally triggered one Saturday morning, instructor Wendy Ross-Atwood just moved her 8:30 class onto the sidewalk, 17 people doing push-ups and lunges to music from her husband's Tesla. What workout would you least want to get caught doing on a public sidewalk?

Breeze Airways now flies nonstop between Burlington and Baltimore/Washington three days a week, with fares advertised as low as $49, and the same plane continues on to Vero Beach, Florida. Which stop would you actually get off at, Baltimore or Vero Beach?

The gunboat Philadelphia sank during the 1776 Battle of Valcour Island and sat on the bottom of Lake Champlain until a diver found the wreck in 1935; the country's oldest surviving warship is now in the middle of a $1.7 million restoration. What do you figure is still down there waiting to be found?

WJOY has been broadcasting since 1946 and just marked 80 years on the air from its home in South Burlington, with host Ginny McGehee inviting longtime listeners in to celebrate. What's the station or show you'd want to stick around for 80 years?

Nineteen-year-old Mustafa Khudaier reopened the kiosk at Church and College as Sabah's House, serving his mother Sabah Abbas's family shawarma recipe after the family came to Vermont as refugees from the Iraq War 12 years ago. What's the one family recipe you'd want to sell out of a Church Street kiosk?

Norman Rockwell paid his Arlington, Vermont neighbors $5 and a cold Coca-Cola to model for his Saturday Evening Post covers, and several of them, including Mary Whalen, the grinning girl with the black eye in "The Young Lady with the Shiner," reunited at the Shelburne Museum this fall. What would it take to get you to model for a famous painter?

The 115-room Sugar House Hotel just opened in Winooski with a maple creemee for every guest at check-in, a café-bar in the lobby and an eighth-floor restaurant looking out over 100 acres of nature preserve along the Winooski River. Café-bar downstairs or the view upstairs, where are you parking yourself first?

Starting Nov. 1, Vermont requires anyone on the open deck of a boat, kayak, canoe or paddleboard to wear a Coast Guard-approved life jacket, a rule that runs through May 1. Which piece of your boat gear needs an upgrade before next season, the jacket, the kayak or the paddle?

Shawn Cliche has filed a zoning application to bring Nectar's back to life on Main Street, using all three floors for food, live music, DJs and pool tables day and night. What's the first show or night you'd want booked there once it reopens?

South Burlington's OnLogic, started at Roland and Lisa Groeneveld's kitchen table in 2003, is being bought by Japan's Omron for $675 million, and every one of its 160 Vermont employees gets a $1,500 bonus for each month they've worked there, which comes to $90,000 for a five-year employee. What would you do with a bonus like that?

Colchester High tenth grader Juliet Wager became the first girl in her troop to reach Eagle Scout by building a Little Free Library-style food and book pantry near Mallets Bay School. What's the one thing you'd stock a free pantry with first?

Burlyaxe Throwing closed its North Winooski Avenue space after seven years and, by its own count, hundreds of thousands of axes thrown, though its mobile trailer is still booking events. What's your record for sticking an axe in the target?

An 11-foot stainless steel sculpture called "Jambo," Swahili for hello, by Enosburg artist David Stromeyer is going into Veterans Memorial Park in South Burlington, donated by resident Todd Lockwood and valued at $80,000. What's the first thing you'd want a giant steel sculpture named "hello" to say back?

Vermont Green FC coach Chris Taylor is stepping down after two years that included a 45-game unbeaten run, a Steinbrecher Cup and back-to-back USL2 national titles. What should the club look for in whoever takes the bench next?

The boat rental and snack bar that ran for decades at Charlie's Boathouse closed in 2021, and now the Winooski Valley Park District has bought the 2.7-acre property at the end of North Avenue, 600 feet of shoreline included, to open as a public park next spring. What would you want there first, a dock, a trail, or just a bench to watch the river mouth?

UVM's Perkins Museum of Geology is open again after a six-year closure, free Monday through Friday, with the Charlotte Whale, Vermont's official state fossil, back on display. What's the one fossil or oddball specimen you'd drag a friend over to see first?

Vermont Pub & Brewery on College Street closes for good on Nov. 14, just days after its 38th anniversary; Greg and Nancy Noonan opened it in 1988, back when there were only 11 brewpubs in the entire country, after Greg helped write the law that made them legal here. What's your pick for a last pint there before it closes?
